issues.failure_explanation: For any $N$ having distinct prime factors such that $\sum 1/p_t \ge 1$ (for example, $N = 30$ with primes $2, 3, 5$ giving $1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 = 31/30$), the definition produces $n_T = 31 > N-1$. An entry $x_{31}$ is out of bounds for a length-$N$ signal indexed in $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. Furthermore, indices are not reduced modulo $N$, and the denominator argument only shows $n_{T_1} \ne n_{T_2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}$, not modulo $N$.

failure_location.quote:
For each subset of indices $T \subseteq \set{1, \ldots, \omega}$, define $n_T = N\sum_{t \in T} \frac{1}{p_t}$. 
We construct a vector ${\bf x}$ with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ as follows.  
For every possible value of $n_T$, let $x_{n_T} = (-1)^{\abs{T}}$,
For all other indices $n$, set $x_n = 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $n_T = N \sum_{t \in T} \frac{1}{p_t} \bmod N$ and add a short argument showing that $\sum_{t \in T_1 \Delta T_2} \pm 1/p_t \notin \mathbb{Z}$ for distinct primes, ensuring $n_{T_1} \not\equiv n_{T_2} \pmod N$.
issues.overall_effect: The construction of the ambiguous signal ${\bf x}$ fails for any composite $N$ whose prime reciprocals sum to at least 1, leaving the base signal used in Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 3.2 invalid as written.
issues.title: Index out of bounds and incomplete injectivity in Lemma 2.2 construction
issues.why_classification: The statement of Lemma 2.2 is a known true result (Pei & Cheng, 2022). Reducing indices modulo $N$ is a routine repair that preserves the statement and all dependent results without new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that $k/d_1$ has a multiplicative inverse modulo $N_1$ because $d_1 = \gcd(k, N_1)$. This is false whenever $\gcd(k/d_1, N_1) > 1$; for example, with $N_1 = 18$ and $k = 12$, $d_1 = 6$ and $k/d_1 = 2$, which shares factor 2 with $18$ and has no inverse modulo $18$. In addition, $h$ in the formula for $n_j$ is undefined.

failure_location.quote:
Since $d_1 = \gcd(k, N_1)$ and $d_2 = \gcd(l, N_2)$, $k/d_1$ and $l/d_2$ must have multiplicative inverses modulo $N_1$ and $N_2$, respectively.
Thus, set $m_j = j(k/d_1)^{-1}p \bmod{N_1}$ for the row index,
and set $n_j = h(l/d_2)^{-1}q \bmod{N_2}$ for the column index.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Observe that $k/d_1$ is coprime to $D_1 = N_1/d_1$ rather than $N_1$, invert $k/d_1$ modulo $D_1$ (and $l/d_2$ modulo $D_2$), and correct $h$ to $j$, which validly solves $m_j k N_2' + n_j l N_1' \equiv jd \pmod N$.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit construction of the solution $(m_j, n_j)$ to equation (3.3) is undefined and fails for general parameters, leaving the claim that each subsignal entry is non-empty unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid modular inverse in Lemma 3.3 proof
issues.why_classification: The claim of Lemma 3.3 is correct, and taking the modular inverse modulo $D_1$ instead of $N_1$ is a standard local repair that preserves the result and all downstream arguments.
